scope: Corollary 10.2 (Consequences under the weaker finite inputs) of the manuscript “Renewal and changes of law for critical honeycomb walks” (preprints/Renewal-and-changes-of-law-for-critical-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d179fa55e4b82fed), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 68-69. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let γ0 be the source port, γn the nth visited vertex of the infinite concatenation, and Yn its forward height from the source. Almost surely, Yn ≥ n3/4−o(1) , |γn − γ0| ≤ n17/18+o(1) . For the normalized finite bridge law summed over heights with weight ρLe−L/n, its height is at least n3/4−ε with probability tending to one, for every ε > 0. The unnormalized mass of half-plane arches 68 of length greater than n is at most n−3/16+o(1). The completed-vertex rewards just defined satisfy, for some fixed C > 0, EVh = h4/3+o(1) , EV (Ch log2 h) h = h4/3+o(1) . (63) Consequently the expected number of vertices before first exit from a disk of radius R is at least R4/3−o(1).
